scope: 51 supplied gaps; bounded changes do not close the entire roadmap

gaps.title: Unresolved exact-division verification counterexample
gaps.progress: Hardware isolates the retained mismatch to emulator FCHK slow-path selection; bounded model repair and deterministic regression. General FCHK truth remains incomplete.
gaps.exit_gate: Replay the exact inputs and emitted sequence on hardware against an independent exact reference, isolate approximation/slow-path/rounding behavior, and retain a deterministic regression before changing verification status.

gaps.title: Full semantic conformance is still a larger task than scalar admission
gaps.progress: Every scalar admission declaration has representative cross-stage fixture records, operand variants and negative controls. Actual Boolean-loop A100 failures now isolate a native predicate guard readiness gap across CFG edges; 2,400 repaired launches and 16,957,440 independent bytes pass under unchanged references. General independent semantics/hardware conformance is still open.
gaps.exit_gate: Maintain one machine-readable cross-stage contract ledger with exact forms, supported operand domains, rejection reasons and independent CPU/toolkit/hardware evidence. Cover combinations and negative controls, rather than counting mnemonics or parser acceptance.

gaps.title: Custom Python types and numerical semantics remain narrow
gaps.progress: Logical Boolean scalar helper arguments/returns now retain exact predicate copies, complete return paths and original source/native signature ownership, with 2,400 A100 launches, 16,220,160 independent complete bytes and 240 exact current native outputs. Physical Boolean launch/storage and narrower scalar ABIs remain open research with original toolkit byte-layout/rejection controls. Typed i64/u64 low64 multiplication and augmented assignment now pass source/helper/loop/cast/square gates with PTX/CUDA controls: 1,560 A100 launches and 156 native outputs. Typed i64/u64 scalar, global/shared array, helper, conversion/comparison/shift routes pass exact gates. Naturally aligned shared arrays charge padding to 48KiB; a failed hardware phase led to bounded native reconvergence and a final 1,280-launch A100 gate. FP64 arithmetic, narrower types and complete Python semantics remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Define the intended typed device-language contract, implement missing types and conversions end to end, and test overflow, rounding, exceptional values and math policies independently. Keep strict FP32, approximate math and half-rounded products distinct.

gaps.title: Reusable Python functions and library calls are not generally compilable
gaps.progress: Pure bool-annotated helper parameters/returns now pass eager once-only argument/effect, predicate loop/early-return, caller isolation and original signature/source/native custody gates: 2,400 A100 launches and 155 new regressions. Original pure scalar early/branch/loop returns now preserve every-path typing, live-path initialization, caller isolation and same-file/imported source ownership with 2,400 A100 launches/240 native outputs. Static same-file/local-package typed scalar helpers support module aliases, relative imports and static re-exports with defining-module annotations, original diagnostics, dependency hashes and native ownership through normal local/remote builds. A 600-launch A100 gate passes; arbitrary runtime packages, captures/host effects and general Python/library/device ABI remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Add typed device-function specialization or inlining with explicit call signatures, captured constants, effect rules and source locations; support separate device calls only with a valid ABI. Test multi-module helpers without executing arbitrary top-level host code during static discovery.

gaps.title: Python objects, containers and compile-time programming lack a general route
gaps.progress: Finite numeric tuple iteration now preserves empty/target/break/continue/nested/else semantics with 2,400 A100 launches and 240 native outputs. Original explicit Final numeric and immutable tuple values now specialize with bounded arithmetic/index/slice/len and exact original source/diagnostic/value/use/ownership. Same-file/imported/re-export/package forms pass 1,440 A100 launches and 144 native outputs; arbitrary objects/runtime containers/metaprogramming/mutable host effects remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Separate compile-time values, host-only effects and device values; admit useful static containers/constants and metaprogramming under explicit specialization rules. Preserve host effects through the application route rather than silently deleting them.

gaps.title: Python control flow is useful but not unrestricted
gaps.progress: Finite static numeric tuple loops preserve empty/observable targets, runtime break/continue, nested tuple/range loops and exhaustion else with original source/type/convergence/ownership. 2,400 A100 launches and 240 native outputs pass. Pure helper early/branch/loop returns now add typed return homes, live-path initialization and caller/source isolation with a separate 2,400-launch A100 gate. Finite i32 range counters now exhaust before wrap; runtime range/while else preserves nearest-loop exits, live-path initialization, convergence and original source ownership in a separate 2,400-launch A100 gate. Typed original condition chains now preserve single evaluation/short-circuit effects, exact pairwise literal contexts and expression/source/native ownership with a separate 2,400-launch A100 gate. Boolean locals/truth/conversions and operand-returning lazy and/or now preserve exact literal contexts, effects and source/native ownership, with an actual hardware predicate-path repair and 2,400 final A100 launches. Arbitrary iterables, dynamic steps, wide bounds, Boolean ABI/type unions and general Python control/effects remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Extend only declared control-flow forms with branch/loop state semantics, defined overflow behavior and convergence checks. Test nested loops, early exits, loop-carried values and long-running bounds through encoding and hardware.

gaps.title: Custom-kernel arrays have no general tensor/view/layout API
gaps.progress: Rank1..4 checked Buffer views admit explicit nonnegative strides, read-only broadcasts and provably nonoverlapping writes, with validated launch bindings. General views, negative strides, alias effects and device layout algebra remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Introduce explicit buffer/shape/stride/alignment and alias contracts, including safe masks and tails. Validate negative/runtime indices, offset overflow, views and external tensor bindings; exploit those facts for code generation without assuming contiguity.

gaps.title: Python GPU primitive vocabulary is incomplete
gaps.progress: Python global i32/u32 atomic_add and u32 exchange/CAS preserve old values, nested evaluation and checked Buffer bounds; A100 contention and convergence gates pass. General collectives, async and tensor primitives remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Connect a typed primitive vocabulary to complete PTX/native contracts, including mask, scope, ordering, synchronization and collective participation rules. Test the Python-to-binary path for every admitted primitive.

gaps.title: Memory safety and shared-memory initialization checks are incomplete
gaps.progress: Checked Buffer accesses implement zero/skip bounds behavior with storage extent, alignment, dtype and write-alias binding validation. Raw pointers remain caller-bounded; shared initialization, arbitrary races and general memory-safety proof remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Declare unsafe versus checked execution; add useful definite-initialization, bounds and synchronization analyses or diagnostics. Use adversarial schedules, masks, dimensions and hardware checking, while preserving explicit rejection where safety cannot be established.

gaps.title: PTX parameter ABI and module grammar are bounded
gaps.progress: Scalar b/u/s8/16 entry parameters now use exact natural byte slots, signed/zero extension and within-slot subword reads across both selectors, interpreter, verifier and public explicit-run/batch-driver ABI. Original PTX A100 gates pass 14,400 launches plus 240 explicit launches, 67,461,120 complete bytes and 240 exact native outputs. Aggregate/vector/FP16/predicate/device-slot ABI and logical Python Boolean launch/storage remain open. Global/generic pointer metadata preserves ABI slots/alignment and ownership. Module-local scalar device functions now retain signatures/body hashes/call counts through validated static expansion and native manifests. Aggregate/register/local/shared-pointer ABI and general linkage remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Implement the needed parameter layout/alignment and pointer metadata, preserve all semantic directives, and account for module symbols and functions across parsing, metadata, launches and linking. Reconcile discovered, parsed, emitted and executable inventories.

gaps.title: Scalar arithmetic/types/modifiers do not cover general CUDA-emitted PTX
gaps.progress: Scalar byte/halfword entry loads now preserve extension/adjacent slots/guarded loop and alias snapshots, with 14,400 original PTX plus 240 explicit-run A100 launches. Actual original CUDA Boolean controls now reach the separately recorded setp.s16/selp.u16 scalar boundary; those narrow register operations remain unsupported. Low64 mul.lo.u64/s64 and typed Python products pass 1,560 original-source A100 launches and 15,974,400 audited bytes, including aliased/guarded/immediate/parameter/helper/loop/cast/square snapshots. Scalar selp.b64/u64/s64/f64 now passes 1,480 original-source A100 launches, 15,155,200 audited bytes and 148 native comparisons; aliases/guards/negation/parameters/immediates preserve bit snapshots. Wide arithmetic/snapshots and literal contexts pass exact gates. Typed integer/floating scalar operand expressions add precedence/casts and binary64 intermediate rounding, with 4,000 independent typed trees, 432 CPU executions and a final 384-launch A100 gate. Failed cross-toolchain controls remain retained with explicit unresolved signedness/NaN/type boundaries; general expressions, arithmetic/modifiers/types/operands and encoder conformance remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Prioritize actual nvcc/custom-kernel blockers, implement exact modifier and type semantics, and prove them with independent bit-level references, same-source ptxas controls and hardware edge cases.

gaps.title: Global/shared memory widths and vector forms remain uneven
gaps.progress: Global v2 loads/v4 stores and scalar narrow/64-bit stores pass byte gates. Scalar shared byte/halfword/64-bit loads/stores add four recovered templates, 12,096 varied native words and a final 1,216-launch A100 gate after retaining a failed barrier schedule. The 336-row width matrix aligns admission/lowering; dynamic shared alignment/initialization/races, vector64 and ordered memory remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Make admission and lowering agree on a published width/type/alignment matrix. Add scalar/vector load/store conversions and tail-safe alternatives, checking address alignment, guards, predication and exact written bytes.

gaps.title: Address spaces and module storage are not generally lowered
gaps.progress: Static per-thread local frames, explicit 32-bit local addresses and scalar32 loads/stores pass 704 A100 launches, exact per-function metadata/resource and ownership gates. G17 adds bounded scalar/group/predicate spill frames. Generic pointers, wider/vector local accesses, device calls and module global/constant relocation remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Define storage placement, address conversion, alignment, initialization and relocation semantics for each supported address space, then validate real module data and per-thread local storage on hardware.

gaps.title: Atomics, reductions and memory ordering are missing compiler foundations
gaps.progress: GPU global 32-bit integer add/exchange/CAS admit relaxed/acquire/release/acq_rel; add reductions remain relaxed. CTA shared 32-bit add/exchange and independent A100 publication/contention gates pass. Full memory-model, scope, width and operation coverage remains open.
gaps.exit_gate: Implement complete operation/type/scope/order contracts with contention, publication/visibility, return-value and inter-block tests. Keep unimplemented ordering combinations rejected rather than treating modifiers as hints.

gaps.title: Warp/block collective and synchronization support is narrow
gaps.progress: Full-mask unpredicated indexed/down/up scalar shuffles admit exact unsegmented clamps, low-five-bit lane operands and reconverged full warps; 1,792 A100 launches pass including aliased operands. Forward scalar CTA phases now receive a hardware-validated BSSY/BSYNC pair where every path provably reaches one barrier. Partial participation, votes/match/redux, cyclic/irreducible convergence and broader barriers remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Add collective participation and mask semantics alongside encoding and scheduling. Validate partial warps, divergent control flow, all barrier participants and memory visibility independently on hardware.

gaps.title: Device calls, call stacks and cross-module device linking are absent
gaps.progress: Direct scalar calls and explicit PTX/CUDA source libraries resolve through static specialization with private/export/weak/signature rules and per-unit dependency/CLI/remote/ownership contracts. A 576-launch A100 gate includes original separately linked controls, wide/local/transitive cases and ordinary CUDA/remote builds. Native object/archive linking, dynamic stacks, recursion/indirect calls and register/aggregate ABI remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Implement a defined call ABI or bounded whole-program inlining/specialization, symbol resolution and stack/local allocation. Test multiple translation units, library calls, recursion policy and resource accounting.

gaps.title: Register/predicate spilling and general pressure management are missing
gaps.progress: Bounded scalar/pair/quad/predicate spills honor explicit and automatic limits. Virtual dependency/guard/order-preserving scheduling admits fewer slots and non-increased block-local transfers/frame. A100 correctness and paired kernel/resource controls pass, including maximum-frame recovery; host code-generation overhead is measured separately. Slot reuse, tensor-fragment spilling and general occupancy policy remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Provide spill/reload and local storage semantics, group-aware allocation and pressure-aware scheduling, including predicates or a safe lowering strategy. Test both correctness and the performance/occupancy effects of imposed register limits.

gaps.title: Tensor instruction and async-pipeline coverage is specialized
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Expand exact instruction, register-fragment, address and synchronization contracts using independent generated inputs. Revalidate dependency schedules and resource limits rather than reusing scalar latency assumptions.

gaps.title: Native GPU architecture coverage remains SM80/A100
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Declare supported target/toolkit combinations, build per-target encoders and machine models, and run conformance, resource, ownership and whole-workload hardware gates on each.

gaps.title: Source-to-binary toolchain independence is incomplete
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: If independence is a product requirement, implement container/metadata/relocation and linking directly, with loadable-binary conformance. Preserve separate internal-backend versus total-toolchain compile measurements in the meantime.

gaps.title: Framework operator coverage is still a small whitelist
gaps.progress: FP32 sigmoid and static rank0..4 sum/mean reductions and backward pass full-state A100/CLI gates. Convolution/pooling and general framework operator/effect coverage remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Build a normalized operator/effect IR with generic faithful lowerings and derivatives, then add optimized recipes. Admit independent CNN, recurrent, transformer, indexing and scientific workloads through the same normal entrypoints.

gaps.title: Model control flow and shapes are static specializations
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Define shape/effect guards, guard-miss behavior and bounded AOT or explicit lazy specialization. Preserve host control flow where appropriate and test unseen values, lengths, branches and recompile/cache behavior.

gaps.title: Model storage/dtype and AMP coverage remain restricted
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Specify dtype promotion, accumulation, cast derivatives, master state and overflow policies end to end. Compare complete training states under the identical policy, including exceptional and small-gradient cases.

gaps.title: Arbitrary strides, aliases and mutation effects are unsupported
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Track base storage, offsets, strides, alias sets and mutation/version effects through capture, differentiation, planning and execution. Test overlapping views, state updates, storage reuse and backward saved-value lifetimes.

gaps.title: Broadcast support is partial and does not extend to batched matmul
gaps.progress: Rank2..4 contiguous batch-broadcast matmul and reduced gradients pass A100; arbitrary rank/layout/operation broadcasting remains open.
gaps.exit_gate: Extend broadcasting as an explicit shape/layout algebra per operation, including inverse gradient reductions and batch products. Validate rank, scalar, singleton and noncontiguous cases without silently expanding precision or storage contracts.

gaps.title: Hard resource bounds exclude common large ML shapes
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Design tiled/split reductions, larger-grid and workspace policies and tail/layout lowerings. Prove resource safety and full forward/backward correctness before raising bounds; measure allocation, padding and compile costs.

gaps.title: Attention feature coverage remains bounded after masked/causal SDPA
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Define each mask/position/head/dropout contract and its derivative/RNG behavior. Test rectangular alignment, fully masked rows, changing masks, head sharing and complete gradients under fixed precision.

gaps.title: Attention is decomposed and materializes quadratic intermediates
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Develop native fused or tiled attention/backward with explicit mask/dropout/precision contracts and shared/register/workspace budgets. Compare complete regions and training steps, including layouts and gradients, against the incumbent.

gaps.title: Embedding does not provide general gather/scatter/index semantics
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Implement each indexing/gradient/alias policy explicitly, including generated indices and invalid-index behavior. Test duplicate indices, empty domains if admitted, sparse updates, padding and mutation effects.

gaps.title: Embedding gradient and broadcast-reduction scaling is a performance gap
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Compare deterministic segmentation/sorting or admitted atomic/reduction policies, parallel sums and sparse updates. Include temporary memory, preprocessing, duplicate distributions and full optimizer semantics in complete-task timing.

gaps.title: Loss support is still MSE plus a narrow cross-entropy contract
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Normalize loss options and reductions with exact target/shape/dtype/invalid-label rules, then validate full loss/seed/gradients and optimizer state. Harmonize public APIs or document their distinct contracts clearly.

gaps.title: Autograd interoperability is first-order and bounded
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Extend derivative/effect IR and lifetime rules for intended higher-order, custom backward, accumulation and checkpointing semantics. Audit every GPU compute launch for composed paths and distinguish interoperable mixed execution from OA-owned training.

gaps.title: RNG, dropout and mutable model buffers remain open
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Introduce explicit RNG and mutable-state ownership/effects, deterministic or declared stochastic policies, derivatives and checkpoint state. Test successive changing steps and resumed sequences against the intended framework semantics.

gaps.title: Optimizer family and option coverage remains limited
gaps.progress: SGD momentum/dampening/Nesterov/decay/maximize and Adam/AdamW AMSGrad/maximize pass complete-state CPU/A100 and resumed trajectories. Parameter groups, clipping/accumulation/schedulers and broader optimizer families remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Add exact equations/options, per-parameter/group state and update ordering, including clipping/accumulation/scheduler interactions where required. Compare moments, steps and every parameter across long trajectories and checkpoint resume.

gaps.title: Optimizer snapshots are not complete application checkpoints
gaps.progress: Owned native programs have versioned complete parameter/buffer/optimizer/CPU-RNG/application-JSON checkpoints with atomic save, staged restore, rollback and exact A100 interrupted/resumed state. Unsupported host, GPU RNG, distributed and AMP state remain separate open contracts.
gaps.exit_gate: Define a versioned complete checkpoint with a consistent update boundary, ownership and compatibility rules. Test interrupted/resumed complete applications, including failure before replacement and all omitted state categories.

gaps.title: Adaptive/indexed training cannot use full CUDA-graph replay
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Choose an explicit graph-safe bounds and step-state design, or document direct-only execution as a lasting boundary. Validate changing labels/indices and bias-correction coefficients over many replays without host work escaping the measured interval.

gaps.title: Indexed runtime validation introduces synchronizing host work
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Measure validation/transfer/host time separately; study native device validation or explicit trusted-input/guard policies only with preserved failure semantics. Confirm no parameter update occurs after an invalid input and include validation in end-to-end claims.

gaps.title: Distributed and multi-device training are not integrated native workloads
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Define the communication/ownership policy and whether vendor communication kernels are allowed, integrate sharded graphs and state, and validate complete multi-device steps including communication and synchronization costs.

gaps.title: KV decoding requires precompiled positive exact-length variants
gaps.progress: Explicit opt-in exact-length specialization validates a native factory, maximum context, build-attempt budget, cache/input/math/parameter guards and failure-preserving adoption. CPU and complete A100 token/cache/ownership gates pass; empty prefixes, padding/position and beam/speculative semantics remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Define bounded dynamic/length-bucket semantics, padding/position handling or explicit lazy specialization, including maximum context and guard misses. Test token-by-token predictions and all caches across supported transitions.

gaps.title: KV cache memory management copies prefixes and lacks paging
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Design storage capacity/page ownership and alias/update rules with attention-position correctness, canaries and reuse tests. Measure decode traffic, memory fragmentation and complete latency over growing contexts.

gaps.title: Production serving behavior is not established by bounded decode tests
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Run independent complete inference applications with fixed model/checkpoint/tokenization/sampling contracts. Measure prefill and decode separately, first-token latency, per-token/tail latency, memory and throughput under declared request/concurrency distributions.

gaps.title: Real build and dependency graphs are not resolved
gaps.progress: Static local Python helper graphs now preserve exact entry/helper/package hashes, original diagnostics, explicit roots and dependency/native ownership through local/remote builds, with 600 A100 launches and public Modal CLI validation. Compilation databases preserve per-source NVCC arguments/cwd/dependency identities and remote rebasing. Explicit scalar source libraries now retain per-unit compilation and deterministic function resolution through CLI/transport, validated against original linked controls. Binary libraries, general build/link orchestration and complete original host application rebuild/execution remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Resolve original build commands and dependency identities in an isolated reproducible environment, including generated source and library linkage. Compare the original and OA builds without altering their intended workload or host behavior.

gaps.title: Custom kernels/operators are not automatically inserted into model execution
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Provide explicit custom-op/device-kernel registration with shape/dtype/layout/alias/effect and backward contracts, preserve launch bindings, and audit all model GPU launches against the native ledger through the ordinary CLI/runtime.

gaps.title: Arbitrary host Python orchestration and environments are not packaged/executed
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Preserve the real entrypoint/arguments/environment and CPU effects while routing GPU work to OA. Validate outputs and complete state for independent repositories; account for CPU work and transfers in end-to-end timing.

gaps.title: General scheduling, tiling and cost models remain incomplete
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Use legal candidate generation with resource/dependency models, independent correctness gates and frozen held-out selection. Optimize real workload distributions and compare both the incumbent and named external controls.

gaps.title: Whole-model fusion, packing and launch planning remain limited
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Compare complete pack+compute+crop and forward/backward/update regions with exact liveness/precision/effect rules. Reduce allocations/traffic/launches only after all storage-view/reuse, changed-input and full-state gates pass.

gaps.title: Cold/warm compilation and cache-hit overhead lack complete attribution
gaps.progress: Source, cache and worker phases now attributed; cold/hit samples retain identical binaries. Remote startup/transport and separate tensor-pass attribution remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Record nonoverlapping frontend/PTX/backend/ptxas/container/disassembly/cache/source/archive/startup/transfer phases for clean and validated warm builds. Preserve raw samples and distinguish remote waiting from compiler time.

gaps.title: Standard reports lack per-kernel steady-state distributions
gaps.progress: Optional repeated profiler audits retain per-contract samples/distributions, loaded resources and binary sizes, with profiler-free whole-step arrays separately labeled. Profiler-free per-kernel performance, fusion and complete host/transfer attribution remain open.
gaps.exit_gate: Provide per-contract repeated samples, medians/spread, launch counts, registers/shared/local memory, cubin/SASS size and graph fusion coverage. Pair profiling with ownership audits and separately measure profiler-free performance.

gaps.title: Full-workload comparisons and compile amortization remain incomplete
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Use identical model/weights/inputs, precision, masks, loss and optimizer state; gate complete correctness first. Compare clean/warm builds, resident and host-inclusive execution, and `build + startup + N*steady_state` per device/toolchain environment, with randomized raw timing samples and named speed ratios.

gaps.title: Independent application and semantic test coverage is still finite
gaps.progress: Original exit gate remains required.
gaps.exit_gate: Maintain independent real-world and adversarial corpora with explicit coverage/rejection matrices, complete state gates and held-out models/shapes. Preserve all source/config/plan/binary hashes, GPU variants, environment versions and failure evidence; never average unsupported cases as slow results.

gaps.title: Regression maintenance still contains a stale rejection and nondeterministic sampling
gaps.progress: Stale bias-broadcast rejection replaced with genuine rejection plus capability control; stable emulator seeds, fixed division case and dtype diagnostics repaired. Tested dependency environments are named; no exhaustive Python/platform matrix claim.
gaps.exit_gate: Update capability/rejection tests together, run the complete supported dependency matrix, and retain deterministic seeds/counterexamples plus random-fuzz seeds. Keep API-specific limits and dated historical reports clearly separated from current support claims.
